speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you are presenting with neck and arm pain, paresthesias, and muscle weakness. To begin our evaluation, please describe exactly where the pain is located and on which side of your neck and arm it occurs.

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; the chronic burning pain and progressive weakness in both hands are concerning. Given your history of diabetes and hypertension, could you please describe if the symptoms radiate from your neck down into specific fingers, and do you have any numbness? Also, have you noticed any difficulty with fine motor tasks, like buttoning a shirt?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of fasciculations, absent reflexes, and progressive weakness alongside sensory symptoms is highly concerning for an anterior horn cell disorder. Given your history of diabetes and the specific distribution of symptoms affecting both hands, do you have any difficulty with swallowing or breathing? REQUEST TEST: Creatine_Kinase, TSH, Vitamin_B12_level, GFR. DIAGNOSIS READY: Amyotrophic_Lateral_Sclerosis
